name: Avon (outside North America)
note: This listing doesn't cover Avon in the US or Canada. Avon there is a different company and isn't certified cruelty-free. Avon International is certified cruelty-free by Leaping Bunny / Cruelty Free International. Its listing names Africa & The Middle East, Asia, Europe and South & Central America. Avon confirmed to me by email that all of its products are vegan, but it has no vegan certification. Regent LP, an investment company rather than a manufacturer, owns Avon in Europe, Asia and Africa (it bought Avon International from Natura, reported as closed in January 2026), and Natura keeps Latin America. Regent has no animal testing policy of its own that applies to Avon. What counts is each brand's own policy. Not sure which Avon you're buying? Check that it comes from one of Avon's sites outside North America, such as avon.uk.com in the UK or avon.co.in in India, and look for the Leaping Bunny logo. Avon's site for the US and Canada, avon.com, isn't covered. Avon's India site says all of its beauty products are approved under the Leaping Bunny programme.

Founded and run by Samantha Brett in Sydney, with a minority investment from XRC Ventures. That PETA listing means its whole range is free of animal-derived ingredients.

name: Emma Lewisham
note: PETA lists Emma Lewisham as cruelty-free, but not as a vegan company. The brand says all its products are vegan except its Skin Shield sunscreens, which contain a small amount of beeswax; it has no vegan certification. I couldn't find it on Leaping Bunny / Cruelty Free International. Founded by Emma Lewisham, and the founders keep the controlling stake.

name: INIKA Organic
note: PETA lists INIKA Organic as cruelty-free and vegan. The brand says its products are cruelty-free and vegan, and shows PETA's cruelty-free mark. I couldn't find it on Leaping Bunny / Cruelty Free International. Owned by Total Beauty Network, an Australian company founded by Tony Rechtman, which also makes Designer Brands cosmetics. That PETA listing means its whole range is free of animal-derived ingredients.

name: BYBI
note: PETA lists BYBI as cruelty-free and vegan. Its own site describes the range as 100% vegan and cruelty-free. In 2021 it said it was Leaping Bunny / Cruelty Free International approved, but I couldn't confirm a current listing. The founders sold the brand in 2024, and the BYBI website is now run by Mystic Elements Limited, a UK company set up in October 2025. That PETA listing means its whole range is free of animal-derived ingredients.

name: Palette
note: Palette is one of Henkel's hair brands, according to Henkel's own UK consumer brands site. Henkel says it doesn't test its hair and body care products on animals, but that animal testing is still mandatory in some countries and it can't rule out that an ingredient was tested at some point. I couldn't find an animal testing policy for Palette itself, and it isn't certified by Leaping Bunny / Cruelty Free International or PETA.
